environment.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 Laptop GPU, 16376 MiB

sglang.reason: SGLang serving dependencies include FlashAttention-4 and a separate Transformers line; keep them out of the pinned M1-C vLLM environment.

notes: The backend is run only from WSL2/Linux; the native Windows .venv is not modified.
vLLM 0.22.1 resolves transformers 4.57.6; the earlier inspected transformers 5.5.3 source snapshot is not the runtime package.
numpy is explicitly resolved at 2.3.5 because the current rLLM/veRL/vLLM metadata has incompatible numpy constraints.
The external flash-attn 2.8.3 wheel is imported from its recorded site-packages path; src/flash_attn is intentionally absent so TraceSearch cannot shadow the third-party package.

vLLM uses its own attention backend in this experiment; the FlashAttention installation primarily resolves the compatible CUDA-extension surface needed by the pinned stack. No rollout speedup is attributed to FlashAttention without profiling evidence.

The first real C0 reached vLLM model load but failed during veRL-to-vLLM dynamic TensorLoRA sync with StopIteration; the merged-LoRA weight-sync mode then reached two real rollout generations. A subsequent veRL batch-postprocessing step exposed the missing optional flash-attn padding helper, now covered by the project compatibility module; no completed C0 training result is claimed until a post-hotfix rerun finishes.
The WSL runner logs the actual EngineCore topology because veRL 0.8 hard-codes the async vLLM server executor backend to mp.
